results.content: This page provides the most accurate and concise summary worldwide for the paper titled Spurious Correlations in Machine Learning: A Survey. ## [Literature Review] Spurious Correlations in Machine Learning: A Survey. [# [Literature Review] Spurious Correlations in Machine Learning: A Survey](/file? Translation, summaries, and formula explanations - all in one AI paper viewer. This paper is a survey about **spurious correlations** in machine learning. **Spurious correlations** are coincidental relationships between non-essential input features and labels, which can negatively impact a model's generalization and robustness when real-world data distributions shift. The paper defines **spurious correlations** formally, categorizes existing methods to address them, and summarizes related datasets, benchmarks, and metrics. * The paper defines a training dataset as *Dtr* = {(*xi*, *yi*)}\*n\*i=1, where *xi* is an input from the input space *X*, and *yi* is a label from the set of *K* classes *Y*. * Each data point *xi* has a **spurious attribute** *ai* from the set of possible **spurious attributes** *A*. * Data with the **spurious correlation** <\*y\*, \*a\*> is assigned a group label *g* = (*y*, *a*) ∈ *G*, where *G* := *Y* × *A* is the set of all possible combinations of class labels and **spurious attributes**. * The paper reviews the standard **ERM** framework and its vulnerability to **spurious correlations**. * The **ERM** objective, because it does not explicitly account for the **spurious attribute** *a*, can lead the model to prioritize the **spurious attribute** *a* if it's an easier feature to learn. * The paper notes that models trained with **ERM** often exhibit poor worst-group test errors, which is formalized as:. * The survey categorizes methods to address **spurious correlations** into four main groups:. - **Causal Intervention**: These methods try to model and exploit the causal relationship between input, label, and the **spurious attributes**. - **Invariant Learning**: Aims to identify features with consistent predictive performance across different domains or groups, avoiding reliance on **spurious correlations**. - **Contrastive Learning**: Encourages the model to learn similar representations for same-class samples, even with varying **spurious attributes**. + Group-label-free **spurious correlation** mitigation.

results.title: Theoretical and Empirical Insights on Learning Under Spurious Correlations and Shortcuts - Yoav Wald
results.content:
Theoretical and Empirical Insights on Learning Under Spurious Correlations and Shortcuts - Yoav Wald
IFML
963 subscribers
4 likes
130 views
12 May 2025
Research talk by Yoav Wald, Faculty Fellow at the Center for Data Science, New York University

Predictive models often exploit spurious correlations, leading to unreliable performance under distribution shift. In this talk, we explore causally motivated approaches to mitigating spurious correlations and improving model robustness. We begin with a simple model for understanding spurious correlations and their impact on generalization. Then we discuss three aspects of developing robust models: (i) Considerations in training overparameterized models that maintain invariance to shifts in spurious correlations, (ii) Approaches to dealing with scenarios where annotations of spurious features are unavailable, (iii) Leveraging large language models and causal estimation techniques to enhance robustness in large-scale, real-world medical text classification tasks.

results.title: Robustness to Spurious Correlations Improves Semantic Out-of-Distribution Detection | Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
results.content: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence. # Robustness to Spurious Correlations Improves Semantic Out-of-Distribution Detection. ## Authors. * Rajesh Ranganath New York University. ## DOI:. ## Keywords:. ## Abstract. Methods which utilize the outputs or feature representations of predictive models have emerged as promising approaches for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection of image inputs. However, as demonstrated in previous work, these methods struggle to detect OOD inputs that share nuisance values (e.g. background) with in-distribution inputs. The detection of shared-nuisance OOD (SN-OOD) inputs is particularly relevant in real-world applications, as anomalies and in-distribution inputs tend to be captured in the same settings during deployment. In this work, we provide a possible explanation for these failures and propose nuisance-aware OOD detection to address them. Nuisance-aware OOD detection substitutes a classifier trained via Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) with one that 1. approximates a distribution where the nuisance-label relationship is broken and 2. yields representations that are independent of the nuisance under this distribution, both marginally and conditioned on the label. We can train a classifier to achieve these objectives using Nuisance-Randomized Distillation (NuRD), an algorithm developed for OOD generalization under spurious correlations. Output- and feature-based nuisance-aware OOD detection perform substantially better than their original counterparts, succeeding even when detection based on domain generalization algorithms fails to improve performance. ## Downloads. ## Published. ## How to Cite. View a PDF of the paper titled Understanding Domain Generalization: A Noise Robustness Perspective, by Rui Qiao and 1 other authors. > Abstract:Despite the rapid development of machine learning algorithms for domain generalization (DG), there is no clear empirical evidence that the existing DG algorithms outperform the classic empirical risk minimization (ERM) across standard benchmarks. Specifically, our finite-sample analysis reveals that label noise exacerbates the effect of spurious correlations for ERM, undermining generalization. Conversely, we illustrate that DG algorithms exhibit implicit label-noise robustness during finite-sample training even when spurious correlation is present. | Cite as: | arXiv:2401.14846 [cs.LG] |. |  | (or  arXiv:2401.14846v2 [cs.LG] for this version) |. results.title: Revisiting Finetuning under Spurious Correlations - NeurIPS 2025
results.content: ## Main Navigation ### Poster ## The Group Robustness is in the Details: Revisiting Finetuning under Spurious Correlations ### Tyler LaBonte · John Hill · Xinchen Zhang · Vidya Muthukumar · Abhishek Kumar ##### East Exhibit Hall A-C #4306 Modern machine learning models are prone to over-reliance on spurious correlations, which can often lead to poor performance on minority groups. In this paper, we identify surprising and nuanced behavior of finetuned models on worst-group accuracy via comprehensive experiments on four well-established benchmarks across vision and language tasks. We first show that the commonly used class-balancing techniques of mini-batch upsampling and loss upweighting can induce a decrease in worst-group accuracy (WGA) with training epochs, leading to performance no better than without class-balancing. Next, we show that scaling pretrained models is generally beneficial for worst-group accuracy, but only in conjunction with appropriate class-balancing. Finally, we identify spectral imbalance in finetuning features as a potential source of group disparities --- minority group covariance matrices incur a larger spectral norm than majority groups once conditioned on the classes. Our results show more nuanced interactions of modern finetuned models with group robustness than was previously known.
